biography_sections.title: 1772 Larne witness and identity limit
biography_sections.markdown:
A manuscript-checked deed dated **12 May 1772** names **Wm Glasgow of Larne** as a witness. It gives no age, occupation or relative, so it cannot distinguish William-1505 from William-3326; its **9 November 1784** registration does not prove survival. The adult 1734–1743 Larne sequence belongs to the older William and cannot be assigned to the 1730 man. No record names William’s father.

Source: [Registry of Deeds, Miller to Drennan, manuscript p. 315, image 166](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-SQLT-3).

biography_sections.title: Joint lessor records, 1736–1757
biography_sections.markdown: The inspected original [memorial 63221](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2) confirms a **10 March 1736** lease, registered 10 April 1738, to William and Hugh Glasgow of Larne for two north-side Newtown tenements. Its named lives are George II, Frederick Prince of Wales and Prince William Augustus, not family members; witnesses include James Stenhouse and William Harrison. A separate [4 June 1757 assignment, memorial 159181](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJX4), manuscript pp.473–474, refers to a head lease granted by William and Hugh Glasgow of Larne. This confirms a joint-lessor association, but neither deed states kinship or names William’s parent, spouse or children.
